content:
lia.sales: ArgosCare POC update — they did a 30m run and saw spikes of 504s when sustained qps hit ~90 and about 12% of requests were >1500 tokens. They want a short 'what we'll run' doc, a rough hosted vs dedicated price delta, and answers for their security questionnaire (KMS + audit). Can we scope a quick benchmark tomorrow?

omar.perf: thanks. that pattern (90 qps + long tail of large prompts) often hits our per-GPU request queueing and occasionally triggers request timeouts when sequence length increases. propose a focused 3-phase benchmark to reproduce and show mitigations.

omar.perf: proposed mini-runbook:
- prep: upload sanitized examples (long/med/short) and set 3rd-party latency monitor; set logging to capture 504 traces
- Phase 1 (baseline, 15m): steady 30/60/90 qps for 5m each with original payload mix (short 55%, med 33%, long 12%)
- Phase 2 (cache warm, 10m): keep 10 qps background + run a 5m burst 120 qps -> hold 3m -> cool 2m
- Phase 3 (config sweep, 20m): test combinations: prefix KV cache on/off, batching window 10/25/50ms, fallback to quantized model for long sequences. Capture p50/p95/p99, 504/5xx rate, GPU queue depth, and tokens/s

omar.perf: lightweight load client (locust-y pseudocode):
```
def task():
    client.post('/v1/chat:generate', json={
        'model':'rwd-chat-4b',
        'messages': sample_payload(),
        'stream': false
    })
```

lia.sales: procurement wants a ballpark: hosted run-rate vs dedicated reserved for this profile (90 sustained). any quick numbers we can surface now?

omar.perf: rough back-of-envelope: with their token mix estimate ~1.3M tokens/day -> hosted usage ~$3.5k/month (on current list rates) for rwd-chat-4b. Dedicated: a small reserved pool (single instance equivalent to 1-2x A100) with tenant isolation -> starting ~$6k/month platform + lower per-token infra. note: dedicated pricing varies with SLAs and audit add-ons. If deterministic latency for bursts is required, recommend dedicated + burst buffer.

sre-jae: ops notes — if they plan to run in our Private/VPC mode, expect ~3-6ms extra network latency depending on customer routing and NACLs. also need customer to whitelabel our load generator IPs for firewall.

security-bot: checklist snippet for questionnaire answers:
- KMS: supported in Dedicated and Private; hosted uses envelope encryption by default and supports enterprise KMS integrations on request.
- Audit logs: full request/response metadata (PII redaction opt-in) available for Dedicated/Private; hosted provides aggregated logs and token-level billing reports.
- Compliance: regional deployment and data residency supported; SOC2 in progress (provide date).

lia.sales: ArgosCare is leaning hosted first. they asked whether we can prewarm caches to avoid first-burst tail spikes. any recommended approach?

omar.perf: prewarm strategy: run a short 5-10 qps warmup with a representative set 10-15 minutes before burst. also validate with smaller steady background (2-5 qps) during production hours. for POC we'll include a warmup phase and show delta in p99.

carlos.prod: FYI, we have a canary build (rwd-chat-4b@canary-1) with improved KV cache eviction; can enable for the POC if desired.

lia.sales: schedule ask — can we do this Wednesday 08:30 PT? ArgosCare stakeholders confirmed that slot.

omar.perf: I can run it and will create a dashboard showing p50/p95/p99, 504/5xx, queue depth, gpu util, and tokens/s. will also capture raw traces for any 504s.

sre-jae: i'll coordinate firewall/IP allowlist and note the Private deployment latency caveat in the invite.

lia.sales: action items:
- omar.perf: prepare locust script + dashboard + brief runbook (today EOD)
- sre-jae: share IPs and prewarm steps, add Private-hosting latency note (tomorrow AM)
- lia.sales: send calendar invite and attach security questionnaire answers from security-bot
- carlos.prod: enable canary KV cache on request for the POC

lia.sales: thanks all — i'll include the rough hosted/dedicated numbers in the invite so procurement has an initial anchor. i'll post the run results in this thread after the session. :smile:
